title: Optimal Incomplete Stepped-Wedge Designs with Observation Costs
banked_reason: The recorded proposal promises a complete all-P support/phase classification, but the all-period branch, positivity, and global-majorant certificates remain absent.
gap_reasons: The recorded proposal promises a complete all-P support/phase classification, but this node remains status:to-prove and its own obligation concedes that the required branch, positivity, and global-majorant certificates are absent.

The advertised complete multi-period design problem is solved only for P=3; for every P>=4, existence and uniqueness of the proposed branches, positivity of their weights, exclusion of additional phases, and global optimality remain open.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact cost-normalized dual, the P=3 phase theorem, a canonical-pattern compression lemma for supplied monotone dual vectors, and high-correlation and finite-budget efficiency guarantees. Two distinct all-period attacks—exact real-algebraic cell decomposition and rational-univariate/Sturm–Tarski certification—reached triangularizations and remainder identities but did not complete even one P=4 branch certificate. The promised all-P existence, uniqueness, positivity, crossing, and inactive-endpoint signs therefore remain open.
tldr: Under the observation-cost and cluster-period-mean model of Hooper and Girling, we derive the exact cost-normalized dual and prove that, for any dual vector already known to satisfy \(0\leq b_0\leq\cdots\leq b_{P-1}\leq1\), its full-pattern sensitivity maximum is attained among \(P+3\) canonical patterns. We determine the \(P=3\) optimizer and phase boundary exactly. For every \(P\geq2\), an explicit sparse design has relative information at least \([1+(1-\rho)(2P-1)^2/(P-1)^2]^{-1}\); after ceiling allocation at any integer budget \(B>2P+2\), its efficiency is at least \((1-(2P+2)/B)/[1+(1-\rho)(2P-1)^2/(P-1)^2]\). The exact support-and-phase problem for arbitrary \(P\geq4\) remains open.
gap: The exact source matching the design universe proves only two periods and explicitly leaves the multi-period solution unproved. Existing staircase theorems optimize continuous observations within a fixed sequence layout, not masses over arbitrary incomplete cluster types, and generic equivalence theory does not supply the required global majorant.
fill: The project seeks a theorem-level all-\(P\) support and phase classification, or an exact counterexample followed by the corrected classification, plus algebraically certified weights, boundary equality cases, comparative statics, a high-correlation benchmark, and implementable integer allocations.
